headline: High: AutoGen’s shell/network/file-write defaults can drive unsafe cross-agent workflows with great_expectations, while shared files create prompt-injection and data-leak paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read and write working-directory files and uses stdin/stdout plus tool calls; great_expectations consumes files for validation results and documentation. If AutoGen writes attacker-controlled content into shared files, great_expectations may parse it as trusted input. The pairwise bridge is documented only indirectly, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to use the same working directory or shared files
IF AutoGen writes content that great_expectations later parses as validation input or documentation
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Add a manual review step before great_expectations reads AutoGen-written files
Prefix AutoGen outputs with machine-readable delimiters and reject free-form instructions
Disable file sharing between the agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen touches application data and can egress broadly; great_expectations reads data sources and stores validation results/documentation. If they share a workspace, sensitive application data can flow from AutoGen into great_expectations outputs or logs. The profiles do not prove a default shared workspace, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or data directory
IF application data passed to AutoGen includes sensitive records
mitigations: Separate input and output directories
Restrict great_expectations to synthetic or redacted datasets
Turn off any unnecessary logging of file contents
Review validation artifacts before sharing them externally
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on the workspace

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen has unrestricted filesystem write and shell execution; great_expectations can install packages and read/write files. Both can mutate the same local environment, so concurrent runs can overwrite artifacts or dependency state. No locking is documented, but the profiles do not show git writes, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF both agents run in the same filesystem namespace
IF either agent writes to shared project files or environment-managed directories
mitigations: Run each agent in its own container or venv
Serialize writes to shared directories
Pin dependencies before either agent runs
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen is a multi-agent orchestration framework that can emit tool outputs and code-execution results; great_expectations produces validation results and documentation. If great_expectations treats AutoGen-generated artifacts as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect tests or reports. The interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF great_expectations consumes AutoGen-produced files or summaries without independent verification
IF downstream automation acts on validation results as if they were ground truth
mitigations: Require human review of AutoGen outputs before validation
Compare AutoGen-generated artifacts against source data
Add schema checks before great_expectations ingests files
Limit downstream automation to read-only reporting
requires-engineering: implement explicit trust boundaries between agents

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen can handle model-provider API keys and broad network egress, while great_expectations is local-network-free and focused on data quality artifacts. A compliance mismatch is possible if regulated data is passed through AutoGen and then persisted in great_expectations outputs, but the profiles do not show a specific residency or certification conflict. Only AutoGen is cited because the risk hinges on its external egress and secret handling.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through AutoGen to an external model provider
IF great_expectations stores validation artifacts containing regulated fields
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of AutoGen prompts
Redact sensitive fields before validation
Store validation artifacts in a compliant location
Review retention settings for both tools
requires-engineering: add policy checks for data residency and retention
